title: Editor Efficiency & Hotkeys ⚡
description: Master the shortcuts that will make you fly through the editor.

slides.title: Why Hotkeys? 🏎️
slides.content:
# Speed Is Power

Professional developers use hotkeys constantly. Every click saved adds up over hours of work.

* Moving your hand to the mouse and back costs **2–3 seconds** each time.
* Multiply by hundreds of actions per day = minutes lost.

Today we’ll learn the **essential** shortcuts every Unreal user must know.

slides.title: Essential Shortcut Cheat Sheet 📋
slides.content:
## Must‑Know Hotkeys

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **W** | Move tool |
| **E** | Rotate tool |
| **R** | Scale tool |
| **Space** | Toggle between Move/Rotate/Scale |
| **Ctrl+Z** | Undo |
| **Ctrl+Y** | Redo |
| **Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V** | Copy / Paste actors |
| **Ctrl+D** | Duplicate selected actor |
| **Delete** | Delete selected actor |
| **F** | Focus on selection |
| **G** | Toggle Game View |
| **F11** | Toggle Immersive Mode |
| **Ctrl+Shift+S** | Save All |
| **Ctrl+S** | Save current level |
| **Alt+2** | Unlit view |
| **Alt+3** | Wireframe view |
| **Alt+4** | Lit view |
| **End** | Snap actor to ground |

quizData.question: Which key toggles between the Move, Rotate, and Scale tools?
quizData.explanation: Pressing Space cycles through transformation widgets: Move, Rotate, Scale.

quizData.question: What does Ctrl+D do?
quizData.explanation: Ctrl+D instantly creates a copy of the selected actor in the same location.

slides.title: Custom Keybindings ⌨️
slides.content:
## Make Your Own

Go to **Edit → Editor Preferences → Keyboard Shortcuts**.

* Search any command (e.g., "Duplicate").
* Click the current binding and press your new key combination.
* Remove a binding by clicking and pressing **Escape**.

You can also import/export keybinding profiles. Many developers share "productivity packs" online.

slides.title: Search Everywhere 🔍
slides.content:
## The Command Palette

Press **Ctrl+P** (or **Ctrl+Shift+P** in UE5) to open the **Command Palette**. Type any command:

* "Create Material"
* "Open Level"
* "Build Lighting"

It’s like Spotlight on macOS or the Run command on Windows – **search instead of navigating menus**.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Learn by Limitation

Challenge yourself: spend 10 minutes with the **mouse turned off** (use only keyboard). You’ll discover shortcuts you never knew existed, and they’ll stick faster.
